tools.name: add_entity
tools.description: Add a new entity to the registry.

tools.description: Upsert a per-source entity identifier.

tools.name: add_relationship
tools.description: Add a new relationship between two entities.

tools.name: ai_search
tools.description:
Default search entry point — call this for fuzzy/natural-language discovery.
Superset of semantic_search/semantic_search_entities/semantic_search_unified
(concepts + entities + cached values); do not call those in parallel with this.

tools.name: auth_events
tools.description:
Identity event stream (crawl_identity_events), newest first: the
login/probe/lease audit trail with the identity (source + account
alias) attached. Same projection the Console auth panel renders.

tools.name: auth_launch_login
tools.description:
Launch a login station for an identity (login-station-console).

Registers/resets the identity as login_required with an egress proxy
(auto-assigned, or the operator's explicit ``proxy:<id>``), then
launches the station (a headful-browser Job + the panel-gated noVNC
observation channel). The login itself happens inside the station: the
operator completes slider/captcha in the panel's embedded view at
``vnc_url`` (RELATIVE — open it through the panel with your own
credential; no token is embedded and the station is reachable only
through the panel). Station status then advances
launching -> waiting_operator -> completed; see ``auth_status``.

tools.name: auth_request_login
tools.description:
Register or reset an identity as login_required (the 需登录队列).

Only writes ``crawl_identities`` + a ``note`` identity_event — the
login itself happens on the login site (headful, via the observation
channel); this tool never executes it. An existing identity is reset
(status -> login_required, lease cleared); a new one is registered
with the given automation level (auto | assisted).

tools.name: auth_status
tools.description:
Authenticated-crawling identity-pool overview.

Per source: identity count, the five-state status distribution
(login_required / active / cooldown / banned / retired) and the
currently-leased count; plus pool-level totals and the in-flight
login-station count (``stations.active`` — launching / waiting for
operator; login-station-console). With ``source``: also the detail
rows for that source's identities (account, status, automation, last
login/success, zero-run streak, lease view) — an unknown source
returns zero totals and empty rows, not an error. Read-only.

tools.name: confirm_binding
tools.description: Confirm a binding in the review queue (provenance -> manual).

tools.name: consume_concepts
tools.description: Seed concept families + variables from the protocol vocabulary.

tools.name: coverage_report
tools.description: Crawl-coverage gap inventory (read-only).

tools.name: crawl_status
tools.description:
Return a structured snapshot of crawl state (on-demand visibility).

Answers "what is the scraw doing / what will it crawl" without a manual
DB query. Datasource-centric, matching the daily digest. Read-only.

tools.name: crossborder_merchant_status
tools.description:
Report merchant-authorization status for a cross-border platform connector.

The inner-ring data channel (store operations, platform bestsellers,
after-sales reviews) is merchant-authorization-gated BY DESIGN: the
connector reads platform OFFICIAL APIs only, with the merchant's explicit
store authorization; scraping is out of contract (triage discipline:
never reverse-engineer). Until a merchant completes authorization the
tool answers with a structured ``unavailable (unauthorized)`` response —
never an error object and never a silent empty list, so agents can report
「不可得（未授权）」 verbatim.

Authorized deployments register merchant grants via the
``FD_CROSSBORDER_MERCHANT_AUTH_JSON`` env ({"<platform>": {"authorized":
true, "merchant_id": "...", "scopes": [...]}}); the same response shape
then flips to ``authorized`` with the granted scopes.

tools.name: data_stats
tools.description:
Observation coverage: a fast aggregate summary, or per-concept detail.

Default (no arguments): an aggregate summary — ``total_concepts``
(catalog size), ``covered_concepts`` (routable and crawled, the same
figure ``coverage_report`` reports), ``concepts_with_observations``
(raw distinct concepts holding rows), ``total_stored_rows``,
``gap_concepts`` / ``stale_concepts``, and a per-entity-type rollup —
plus a ``stores`` section from the latest data census (local master
exact + each shard's catalog-based estimate, chunk count, data
time-range end). ``total_stored_rows`` counts stored ROWS: sources
coexist per point, so two sources on one point count twice; the
per-concept listing below counts distinct observation points instead.

The per-concept listing (point count, latest date, distinct sources,
most recent fetch) is returned only when narrowed — pass ``concept_id``
or ``entity_type`` for a filtered listing, or ``detail=True`` for the
unfiltered one. That listing sweeps the observations table and is
deliberately not the default.

Read-only: census rows are READ, never collected (refresh via the panel
action or the ``census`` CLI). The same data powers the panel's
``/panel/data`` page.

tools.name: enumerate_wbgapi_indicators
tools.description: Enumerate all WDI indicators into columns + concepts + bindings (idempotent).

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Force a fetch for one (concept, entity, date), bypassing cache freshness.

tools.name: flower_company_financials
tools.description:
Read a flower company's quarterly financials and flower revenue share
(read-only).

Stored concepts: ``financials.revenue`` / ``financials.operating_profit``
/ ``financials.net_income``. The flower revenue share comes from the
universe row: ``flower_revenue_share`` is ``null`` when disclosure was
not obtained, and the payload then carries ``share_unavailable_reason``.
``null`` is never rendered as 0 and never ranked.

Segment figures and consolidated figures are **not** additive; this tool
returns consolidated financials only and says so.

tools.name: flower_planted_area
tools.description:
Read AIPH planted-area cross-sections (read-only, annual, hectares).

Every row carries its **own** reference year (``ref_year``, extracted
from the observation date) because the yearbook mixes editions inside
one workbook (2005–2024). The payload is therefore a cross-section: no
growth rate is computed, and a per-product year range is reported so a
caller cannot mistake it for a time series.

tools.name: flower_price_series
tools.description:
Read one Dounan commodity item's daily market prices (read-only).

Calibers are three separate published values (``avg`` / ``high`` /
``low``); the average is *not* derived from high/low. The unit comes
from the item entity (元/枝 or 元/把) because one concept covers both —
averaging across items is therefore forbidden, and this tool never does
it.

Missing days are missing: the payload reports ``missing_dates`` inside
the item's observed span and never interpolates or zero-fills.

tools.name: flower_trade
tools.description:
Read flower HS6 trade tiers (read-only, annual, USD).

Three tiers exist and are **never merged** (merging hides the product
mix): ``060311`` fresh roses, ``060319`` other fresh cut flowers,
``060120`` bulbs/corms/tubers in growth. ``0602`` live ornamental plants
is a different structure and is not part of this surface.

Export and import are separate flows on purpose: subtracting one from
the other mixes FOB and CIF valuation, so the payload reports each flow
and never derives a net figure here.

tools.name: flower_universe
tools.description:
List the registered flower universe with per-lane availability.

Read-only. Returns three groups registered under one universe tag: the
7 monitored listed companies (``pure-flower`` / ``adjacency`` tiers), the
23 Kunming Dounan commodity items, and the 8 countries that appear in
the AIPH planted-area chapter. Every lane carries either a real row
count or an explicit unavailable reason — never a zero-valued
substitute for "not obtained".

tools.name: generate_refresh_schedules
tools.description: Generate cron schedules for concepts from their indicator_defs.frequency.

tools.name: get_entity
tools.description:
Look up one entity by exact type+code (ticker AAPL, country CN).
Use when the code is known; do not use search tools for this.

tools.name: graph_search
tools.description: Perform graph-based entity relationship queries using NetworkX.

tools.name: hotel_benchmark
tools.description:
Industry benchmark side of a hotel comparison — **always unavailable**.

This tool exists so callers receive a sentence instead of zeros: the
only industry benchmark sources (STR / CoStar) are paid and are not
wired into this platform. It never returns a peer average as a
substitute, and never returns 0.

tools.name: hotel_company_events
tools.description:
Read one company's disclosure events (read-only, event plane only).

HKEX title events and SEC EDGAR filing events. No headline numbers are
extracted from announcement bodies (they are structure-less PDFs), so
this tool never invents revenue or profit from a title.

tools.name: hotel_kpi
tools.description:
Read one company's RevPAR / ADR / occupancy readings (read-only).

Returns every stored point for the company with ``source_used``,
``granularity``, ``as_of`` and the caliber note. Companies whose market
has no lane (EU) or whose carrier is limited return an explicit
``unavailable`` block naming the reason — never another company's
numbers.

tools.name: hotel_series
tools.description:
Read one hotel series by concept code (read-only).

Covers the star-rated quarterly survey (``hotel.cn.star_rated.*``),
domestic tourism demand (``hotel.cn.tourism.*``) and EU accommodation
(``hotel.eu.*``). Every point carries ``source_used``; the payload
carries ``as_of``, the caliber caveats and the period count. A concept
with no rows returns an explicit ``unavailable`` block, never an empty
list pretending to be a coverage gap.

tools.name: hotel_universe
tools.description:
List the 33-company hotel universe with per-company lane coverage.

Read-only. Each company carries its region, segment, ticker and the
lanes that actually feed it; a company whose market has no lane (EU) or
whose carrier is limited (TW snapshot-only, JP no lane) carries an
explicit ``unavailable`` entry with the reason — never an empty list.

tools.name: import_catalog
tools.description: Import one (by name) or all fd-* provider registries into the catalog.

tools.name: import_crosswalks
tools.description: Ingest the shipped crosswalk registry (crosswalks/*.yaml) as mappings.

tools.name: list_bindings
tools.description: List column->concept bindings (optionally filtered by concept code).

tools.name: list_cnreport_rules
tools.description: Browse cn-report's extraction rules (llm_rules + script_rules).

tools.name: list_concept_families
tools.description:
List the concept families (the curated semantic vocabulary) + variable counts.

Paginated with the same ``limit`` (1..1000) / ``offset`` semantics as
``list_concepts``, ordered by family code.

tools.name: list_concept_mappings
tools.description: List concept mappings forward (by Variable) or in reverse (by external term).

tools.name: list_concepts
tools.description:
List concepts (Variables) with their concept family; optionally filtered.

Paginated: rows are ordered by (entity_type, code, id) and a page returns at
most ``limit`` rows (clamped to 1000). Page with increasing ``offset`` until
a page comes back shorter than ``limit`` — that enumerates the full catalog
even when one entity type exceeds the per-call cap.

The catalog also serves verified entries of the unified indicator registry
(world_bank / gta_panel / china_city_panel / fd_open_data mirror sources).
Registry rows are appended after the native rows, ordered by
(domain, semantic_code); they carry additive ``native_code`` and
``source_db`` fields, so an entry is findable by either identifier, and a
``read_via`` hint naming the domain tool that serves its values. Reading
a registry-only indicator: pass its semantic_code (or native_code) as
``concept_id`` to ``read`` / ``read_series`` — the read routes
transparently through the indicator's source-database read channel.
Entries whose semantic_code duplicates a non-deprecated native concept
code are deduped (native row wins); deprecated legacy rows never shadow a
verified entry.

tools.name: list_entities
tools.description: List entities of a specific type.

tools.name: list_registry_entries
tools.description:
Enumerate the WHOLE unified indicator registry — verified AND not.

The registration-surface enumeration channel (tiered browsing sync, e.g.
the public indicator catalog): every registered entry, each carrying its
authoritative ``verified`` flag (true = directly readable caliber,
false = registered/on-demand caliber). This is deliberately PARALLEL to
the catalog: ``list_concepts`` / ai_search / read keep their verified
gate untouched — unverified entries stay out of the catalog, search and
every read channel, and this tool does not change that.

Paginated like ``list_concepts``: rows ordered by (source_db, native_code),
``limit`` clamped to 1..1000; page with increasing ``offset`` until a page
comes back shorter than ``limit`` — that enumerates the full registry
(57k+ entries at ~1000/page).

tools.name: list_relationships
tools.description: List relationships for an entity.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List all refresh schedules.

tools.name: plan_crawl
tools.description:
Plan a concept crawl -> CrawlPlan artifact (concepts in, methods out).

Compiles desired concepts + entity scope + date range into a ranked, failover-aware
CrawlPlan. Does not fetch. Unroutable concepts (no confirmed binding) and unmapped
entities (no per-source identifier) are reported, not silently dropped.

If ``since_last`` is True, the plan's ``date_range.start`` is derived from the minimum
per-concept ``max(date)`` already in ``semantic_observations`` (incremental crawl).
Either ``start`` or ``since_last`` must be provided. If both, ``start`` wins.
``end`` defaults to today if not provided.

``mode`` is ``per_date`` (one request per concept x entity x date) or ``series``
(one request per concept x entity against a bulk_history endpoint; the pipeline
explodes the returned frame). Series mode refuses concepts bound only to non-bulk
functions.

tools.name: platform_cancel_pending
tools.description:
Cancel a pending platform run (pending_runs row). CAS: only rows
still pending/claimed can be cancelled; terminal rows return an
explanation, unknown ids {"status": "not_found"}.

tools.name: platform_cancel_run
tools.description:
Request cancellation of a RUNNING platform run (sets the
cancel_requested flag; the runner terminates as cancelled at its next
checkpoint). Terminal runs return an explanation, unknown ids
{"status": "not_found"}.

tools.name: platform_runs
tools.description:
Platform run history from ``crawl_runs`` (all member sites), newest
first, with the pending_runs trigger lineage (requested_by) when the
run was started from the control plane.

tools.name: platform_sources
tools.description:
Crawl-platform source inventory with health and stall hints.

Every source mirrored into ``crawl_sources`` (content-repo manifests +
federation members), each with: site, schedule (null = registered but
not lit), enabled, the latest ``crawl_runs`` status/time/rows_written,
the active pending-run count, and a ``stalled`` hint (a lit, enabled
source with no run record for >7 days). Read-only.

tools.name: platform_trigger
tools.description:
Trigger an immediate platform run for ``source`` (insert pending_runs).

Same validation and guardrails as the panel's trigger button: the
source must be registered in crawl_sources and enabled, and single-
flight applies (refused while an open run exists). Returns
{"status": "triggered", "pending_id": ...} or a clear refusal text.

tools.name: policy_create
tools.description: Create a crawl policy.

tools.name: policy_delete
tools.description: Delete a crawl policy and all its runs (cascade).

tools.name: policy_disable
tools.description: Disable a crawl policy.

tools.name: policy_enable
tools.description: Enable a crawl policy.

tools.name: policy_estimate
tools.description:
Estimate the fetch count for a policy payload (used by the panel editor).

Returns {"estimate": int, "unroutable": [...], "unmapped": [...], "policy_max_fetches": int}.

tools.name: policy_get
tools.description: Get a single crawl policy by ID.

tools.name: policy_list
tools.description: List crawl policies. Optional filter by enabled status.

tools.name: policy_runs
tools.description: List policy runs. Optional filters: policy_id, status (running/success/failed).

tools.name: policy_trigger_now
tools.description:
Trigger a crawl for the policy immediately.

Bypasses the cron schedule but still enforces single-flight (skips if
an open run exists) and the plan-size guardrail (refuses if estimate
exceeds POLICY_MAX_FETCHES unless force=true).

tools.name: policy_update
tools.description: Update a crawl policy. Only provided fields are changed.

tools.name: propose_bindings
tools.description: Propose column->concept bindings (propose-and-confirm; below-threshold withheld).

tools.name: rank_sources
tools.description: Rank candidate sources for a concept (best-first) with composite scores.

tools.name: re_embed_concept
tools.description: Re-embed a single concept.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read a concept for an entity over dates (read-through cache + ranked dispatch).

Local concepts: concept_id is the numeric id; entity_type/entity_id/dates
are required; ``source`` pins the read (and any dispatch) to one source;
``all_sources`` returns every held row per date, best-ranked first, without
dispatching — for cross-source comparison.

Registry-only indicators (catalog rows with id=None): pass the
semantic_code (or native_code) as ``concept_id`` — the read is routed
transparently through the indicator's source-database read channel and
returns the same row shape; ``entity`` carries the region/country/city
name when the channel needs one (world_bank requires it). Provenance
travels in ``source_used``.

``scope`` (optional): restrict this call to a named retrieval scope — an
indicator outside the scope returns an explicit out-of-scope response;
the reserved name ``unscoped`` forces the full corpus.

tools.name: read_series
tools.description:
Read a series for one concept x entity over [start, end].

Local concepts (numeric ``concept_id``): serves the stored cache only,
highest-ranked source per point, ordered by date. It NEVER dispatches
upstream — an empty window is a coverage fact reported as such, not a
failure. Use ``read`` for a point read (cache + live dispatch) or
``fetch`` to force a refresh of one point.

Registry-only indicators (semantic_code / native_code as ``concept_id``):
the window is routed transparently through the indicator's source
database read channel (same response shape; ``entity`` carries the
region/country/city when the channel needs one). Provenance travels in
each point's ``source_used``.

``scope`` (optional): restrict this call to a named retrieval scope —
out-of-scope indicators return an explicit out-of-scope response; the
reserved name ``unscoped`` forces the full corpus.

tools.name: record_concept_mapping
tools.description: Assert that a Variable maps to an external vocabulary term.

tools.name: register_datasource
tools.description: Register a datasource manifest into the ontology database.

tools.name: register_discovered
tools.description: Auto-discover + register manifests from entry points + a datasources/ dir.

tools.name: resolve_entity
tools.description:
Resolve an entity <-> per-source identifier, in either direction.

Forward (entity -> identifier), the default:
    resolve_entity(entity_type="country", entity_id=1, source="worldbank")
    -> {"identifier": "CN"}   (or null when that source has no mapping)

Reverse (external anchor -> entity), pass `identifier` instead of the
entity: `wikidata` (QID, e.g. Q148) and `datacommons` (DCID, e.g.
country/CHN) are the anchor sources.
    resolve_entity(source="wikidata", identifier="Q148")
    -> {"match": {"entity_type": "country", "code": "CN", ...}}
    An identifier no entity carries returns {"match": null}, not an error.

tools.name: restaurant_company_events
tools.description:
Read a restaurant company's disclosure events (read-only).

Sources currently registered: HKEX 披露易 title events
(``source_used = hkex-disclosure``, date = ``release_date``) and SEC
EDGAR company-facts events (``source_used = sec-edgar-facts``, date =
``filed``). Each event carries ``source_used``, ``disclosure_date``
and ``doc_url``. Rows are deduplicated by upstream document key.
Companies without an event lane return an explicit ``unavailable``
block with the region-specific reason, not an empty list alone.

tools.name: restaurant_company_financials
tools.description:
Read a restaurant company's quarterly financial observations.

Concepts: ``financials.revenue``, ``financials.operating_profit`` and
``financials.net_income`` (a short name ``revenue`` /
``operating_profit`` / ``net_income`` is also accepted). Each point
carries ``source_used`` (``sec-edgar-facts`` for US names, the
existing A-share lane for CN) and ``as_of``. HK headline figures are
only in announcement PDFs and are not structured; JP and TW lanes are
not connected — those return an explicit ``unavailable`` block per
concept with the established reason. SEC names below the 24-period
gate (BROS; QSR net income; TXRH net income) are reported as
``期数不足未入库``, never as an empty series.

tools.name: restaurant_sampling_notices
tools.description:
Read SAMR food-inspection notices (event plane only, read-only).

Returns the individual notices from the SAMR sampling-notice feed
(``source_used = samr-food-inspection``) with notice date, URL,
result category and whether the notice is restaurant-related. This is
an event plane: no monthly counts or rates are returned here, because
an aggregate would be a read-time statistic, not an upstream
observation series. A category with no rows is reported as an explicit
no-match note, not as a fake zero series.

tools.name: restaurant_series
tools.description:
Read one macro / cost-chain series by concept code (read-only).

Covers the curated restaurant series (NBS catering revenue, Census
food services, FAO food price index, hog/pork prices, DCE meal and
corn, IMF palm oil / sugar, USDA beef and cattle inventory, RPI,
Eurostat catering HICP) plus the US CPI comparison pair
``price.cpi.us.food_away_from_home`` / ``price.cpi.us.food_at_home``.
Every point carries ``source_used`` and ``as_of``. An unknown or
empty series returns an explicit ``unavailable`` block; it is never an
empty list pretending to be a coverage gap.

tools.name: restaurant_universe
tools.description:
List the registered restaurant universe with per-lane availability.

Read-only. Returns the 35 monitored listed restaurant companies with
region / segment / ticker / lanes and, for every lane, whether the
store holds data or the lane is currently unavailable and why. An
unavailable lane carries the explicit reason (EDINET key missing, TWSE
snapshot-only 月营收 without a profit/event face, headline numbers only in
HKEX PDFs, SEC periods below the observation gate) — never a zero-valued
substitute.

tools.name: review_bindings
tools.description: Return the below-threshold review queue (propose-and-confirm).

tools.name: run_schedule
tools.description: Run one refresh schedule now (ranked-failover dispatch + execution record).

tools.name: scope_bind_caller
tools.description:
Bind a caller's default scope (applies when the caller passes no
explicit scope; an explicit parameter — or the reserved ``unscoped`` —
always wins). ``caller_key`` is opaque: the ``X-FD-Caller`` request
header value for HTTP callers, or the FD_MCP_CALLER_KEY env identity for
integrations.

tools.name: scope_create
tools.description:
Create a named retrieval scope.

rules: allow-lists over the registry dimensions —
``{source_dbs: [...], domains: [...], semantic_codes: [...],
native_codes: [...]}`` (every list optional; a scope with no allow-lists
is rejected). Allow-list values are validated against the live
registry_entries/concepts tables: a scope matching nothing known is
rejected; the number of matched indicators is returned. ``unscoped`` is
reserved. Scope is a precision/cost tool, not a permission wall.

tools.name: scope_delete
tools.description: Delete a scope (its caller default bindings go with it; stats remain).

tools.name: scope_list
tools.description: List every retrieval scope with its allow-list rules.

tools.name: scope_list_bindings
tools.description: List caller default-scope bindings (optionally one caller's).

tools.name: scope_stats
tools.description:
Per-day hit counters for one scope (calls, results_returned), most
recent first — the cost-savings evidence (spec「Scope effectiveness is
observable」). An unknown scope is an explicit error naming it.

tools.name: scope_unbind_caller
tools.description: Drop a caller's default scope binding.

tools.name: scope_update
tools.description: Update a scope's rules and/or description (same validation as create).

tools.name: seed_entity_identifiers
tools.description: Seed akshare/yfinance (stocks) and worldbank (countries) identifier mappings.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description:
Search concepts semantically using vector embeddings.

Returns {cached, count, results}: results are the matching concepts with
scores, ordered by similarity; cached=true marks a TTL-cache hit. Pass
``scope`` to constrain retrieval to a named scope (see scope_list); a
scoped response names the scope that governed it.

tools.name: semantic_search_entities
tools.description: Search entities semantically using vector embeddings.

tools.name: semantic_search_unified
tools.description: Unified semantic search across both entities and concepts.

tools.name: update_binding
tools.description: Update concept binding confidence/provenance/review status.

tools.name: update_concept
tools.description: Update concept metadata (name, verification status).

tools.name: update_entity
tools.description:
Update or create an entity in the ontology database.

This is an admin tool for updating entity metadata after initial registration.
